column12: 1231 7 Aug; 1 heavy cruiser, 3 light cruisers, 1 destroyer, course 270, speed 30 as reported
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.70-71 (ch.V(g)) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)

column10: St George's Channel, off Cape St George
column12: 1937 two "destroyers" sighted; 1942-1945 ships passed very close; 2000 trailed
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.68 (ch.V(e)) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: S-38 mistook the two light cruisers for destroyers and counted three larger ships (really five heavy cruisers). Too close to fire torpedoes. Reported by radio.

column12: 2222 large submarine bearing 250, about 5 miles, high speed
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.68-69 and 82 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Reached CTF 62 at 0700 8 Aug (ch.V p.68) or 0710 (ch.VII p.84): a Bates internal difference of ten minutes. CTF 62 alerted TF 62 to a submarine.

column12: dispatch 071219 (GCT); broadcast 2319 per Bates
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.71 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Report of the 1231 B-17 contact was not broadcast until 2319, a delay of 11 h 29 min per Bates.

column12: received by CTF 62 about 2400 7 Aug
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.53 and 71 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Report with two items: B-17 contact on four cruisers and a destroyer north of Rabaul, and a contact on six unidentified ships in St George's Channel heading southeast. Bates: because of heavy traffic at Rabaul it would not have shown a southward movement.

column12: COMSOWESPAC dispatch 071930; broadcast 0730 8 Aug; received by SOPAC commanders 0738 8 Aug
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.68 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: S-38 contact reached the SOPAC commanders 11 h 38 min after it was made. Bates ch.VII says CTF 62 had the S-38 report at 0710 for the separate large-submarine sighting (2222 7 Aug), and passed it to TF 62. The two reports are different items.

column12: 1026 report, 3 heavy cruisers, 3 destroyers, 2 seaplane tenders or gunboats
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.102 (ch.VII(f)) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates time of contact 1026. Bates says force was really 5 heavy cruisers, 2 light cruisers, 1 destroyer. Japanese side (Bates ch.VI p.73): CHOKAI and CRUDIV 6 sighted a Lockheed bomber at about 1020 and shot at a later Hudson at 1110. The two times (1020 Japanese sighting of plane and 1026 Allied contact) are different events.

column12: 1020 one ship sighted a Lockheed; CHOKAI sighted plane 6 min later
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.73 (ch.VI) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Japanese warships saw the Hudson. The cruiser force twisted course to confuse the shadower. CHOKAI opened fire on a second Hudson at 1110 (about 1100 CRUDIV 6 saw a second Hudson); it vanished about 1115.

column12: 1101 two heavy or light cruisers and one unidentified vessel
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.102-103 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates thinks the pilot saw only the three ships that had not been recovering planes. Bates says the report reached COMSOPACFOR about ten and one-half hours after it was made; the OCR of the clock time is garbled.

column12: Pearl Harbor Fox schedule received 1645-1646 by CTF 62; CTG 62.6 1645 Fox and 1657 BELLS
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.102 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: the 1026 Hudson report reached the responsible commanders about 8 h 20 min after contact. Path was Fall River, Port Moresby, Townsville, Brisbane (COMSOWESPAC dispatch 080717 GCT, i.e. 1817 zone -11), Canberra, Pearl Harbor. Bates quotes Pearl Harbor completing the Fox broadcast at 1845 zone -11 and CTF 62 receiving it between 1645 and 1646: Bates's own times are internally inconsistent in OCR; treat the receipt time as uncertain.

column12: ONI: Turner diary 1800; broadcast again 1821 from Melbourne; Astoria 1800-2000 watch; Quincy chief radio electrician 1600
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-Savo/USN-CN-Savo-1.html (footnote 2)
column19: ONI footnote lists several times the 1126-1130 sighting (3 cruisers, 3 destroyers, 2 gunboats at 05-49S 156-07E) reached ships. Some crew of Vincennes slept beside their guns. Compare Bates 1645-1646 and 1900 rows.

column12: Special Instructions to Screening Group (about 1830; Bates cites para 3(b) and 6)
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.54-57 (ch.V(b)) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Each group acts independently if both are attacked; destroyers concentrate on their senior if told; striking force five miles NW of Savo (excluding BLUE and RALPH TALBOT). Pickets: report at once, shadow, report frequently. ONI ch.2 adds night orders stressed alertness, all-round lookout, and submarine warning.

column12: night screening disposition taken at 1850
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.88 and 55-59 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Three cruiser groups plus two radar/anti-submarine pickets. Bates: pickets told to report and shadow, and possibly illuminate with searchlights; no provision for surprise raid detected only within gun range. COMSOPAC later criticised the shadow and searchlight instructions.

column12: Condition TWO
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.111 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: BLUE in American Condition II on station 9-05S 159-42E to 9-09S 159-37E (ONI gives 159-24E for one point as typographical error); courses 051 and 231 at 12 kn. Visibility as reported by BLUE about 3000 yd (OCR "8000"; text says Japanese saw 11000): see conflicts.

column12: Condition TWO until 0148 general quarters
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.112 and 147 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Line between 8-59S 159-55E and 9-01S 159-49E, courses 072 and 252 at 12 kn.

column12: about 1900 per Bates
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.88 (ch.VII(a)) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates ch.VII: at about 1900 CTF 62 received (via Pearl Harbor Fox) the 1026 report as seaplane tenders or gunboats plus two submarines at 1127 (actually one, I-121). This is a different time from 1645; Bates states both. Disputed within Bates.

column12: started patrolling the channels either side of Savo Island at 1915; Condition of Readiness II
column14: https://www.history.navy.mil/research/histories/ship-histories/danfs/b/blue-i.html (8 August 1942)
column19: The entry also says Crutchley had been told the pickets' radar was good for 12 to 14 miles, that the crews were new to the set, and that Blue's lookouts were tired and watching for Cape Esperance

column12: conference called at 2045; held about 2326/2346 (OCR); Marine general went ashore 2346
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.88-90 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Conference agreed enemy force reported off Bougainville was bound for Rekata Bay (seaplane base). Decision made to withdraw transports at 0600 if possible. Bates also: Turner thought the enemy would not attack a stronger force. ONI ch.1 says conference held about midnight.

column12: 2055 CTG 62.6 told Capt. Bode of CHICAGO to take charge of the AUSTRALIA group
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.89-90 (ch.VII(a)) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Crutchley took AUSTRALIA to the McCawley conference. He told CHICAGO's CO he might not return that night. Bates says he did not tell Capt. Riefkohl (Vincennes) or give him command. Bates: CHICAGO's CO did not take the lead (stayed at the rear) and CANBERRA kept the lead.

column12: VINCENNES group not told of Crutchley's absence
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.90 and 142-148 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: Riefkohl did not know AUSTRALIA had left the group nor that he was officer in tactical command of the western screen. He learned Crutchley was absent only later (he stated three years after he did not know). ONI ch.2 notes Crutchley said that if attacked each cruiser group acts independently.

column12: 2123 CO CHICAGO directed the formation to remain as it was with CANBERRA leading
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.90 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Course changes by column movement about every even hour. Bates gives reasons why CHICAGO did not lead: fatigue, no staff, expecting AUSTRALIA to return.

column12: left formation for a command conference at 2130
column14: https://www.history.navy.mil/research/histories/ship-histories/danfs/b/bagley-iii.html (8 to 9 August 1942)
column19: A third time for Australia leaving the southern group. The 1950 analysis gives 2055 in one place and 2125 in another

column12: COMSOWESPAC 060647 GCT; reached SOPAC forces about 2136 zone -11
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.89-90 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Second Hudson report (1101: 2 cruisers one similar to Southampton class, and a small ship). Bates cannot say whether CTF 62 or CTG 62.6 received it; at least one subordinate (Vincennes) mentions it.

column10: north, 34 miles per report relayed on JS circuit
column12: about 2300 SC radar contact bearing north, 34 miles (footnote 5, ONI)
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-Savo/USN-CN-Savo-4.html (Warnings and footnote 5)
column19: ONI says it is not clear whether it was a ship or plane; most likely a plane. Radar plot ensign said the set was swept 360 with serious land interference on all sides and nothing unusual was noticed on a 30,000-yard scale.

column12: crew fatigue: two days of constant combat
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.90, 105, 142 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: personnel worn out after two days in the area; no flag officer present; no battle plan; night attack not anticipated by the high command. Turner, in his own account quoted by Bates, thought the enemy force would not attack a stronger force.

column12: 2315 two planes launched, one from AOBA and one from KAKO
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.77 (ch.VI) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: To lay a marker for the cruiser force, scout and report, and illuminate the transports when CHOKAI was 20 miles off. At 2335 CRUDIV 18 sighted a marker lamp bearing 140; the marker was dropped about 30 miles from Cape Esperance bearing 140. At 2342 Mikawa saw a light bearing 126 over Tulagi.

column10: low over Savo island, heading east
column12: 2345 (ONI); 2346? Bates OCR
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.90 (ch.VII) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Warned on TBS and TBO: plane over Savo headed east. Heard by BLUE, PATTERSON, VINCENNES, QUINCY. Neither CTF 62 nor COMDESRON FOUR answered; COMDESDIV EIGHT tried to relay but failed. Crutchley did not hear until about 0150.

column12: 2345 plane over Savo headed east
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-Savo/USN-CN-Savo-4.html (Warnings)
column19: ONI: also San Juan reported aircraft flying east from Savo by TBS about the same time. BLUE picked up the plane on radar after the warning. Quincy radar picked it up; bridge told control to disregard 5-10 min later.

column12: Chicago, Patterson, Bagley American Condition II; CANBERRA British Condition II modified
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.111 and 125 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: American Condition II means half the armament and all fire control and communications manned. CANBERRA: half guns fully manned, half crews sleeping near their quarters; gunnery communications awake. ONI ch.3: CANBERRA turrets B and Y not manned, one 4-inch each side manned, all guns empty; Chicago state not reported.

column12: detected plane over Savo only after Ralph Talbot's warning
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.111 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: BLUE's radar had detected a cruiser plane over Savo about half an hour before 0100 but only after being alerted; it failed to detect surface ships.

column12: 0025 signals: "Three heavy cruisers south of Savo, course 290, speed 18" and "Prepare to fire torpedoes"
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.106 (ch.IX) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Report from a floatplane. Bates: CHICAGO group actually two cruisers and two destroyers on 306 at 12 kn. Source is USSBS interrogation of Capt Kato (Nav 83, p.361), citing Bates.

column10: west of Savo, Blue on radar picket
column12: about 0053, destroyer bearing 162; range 10,900 yd (Diagram K) or 8,700 yd (p.111)
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.107 and 111 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: The 1950 analysis prints two ranges for this sighting: 10,900 yards on p.107, read off its Diagram K, and 8,700 yards on p.110. Both pages were checked against the page images and both are as printed. The analysis does not reconcile them.

column12: At about 0053 she was sighted by the CHOKAI bearing 162 distant 8700 yards (p.110)
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.111 (ch.X(a)) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: The second range the 1950 analysis prints for the same sighting, on p.110 in its account of Blue: about 0053, bearing 162, distant 8,700 yards. See the row for 10,900 yards. Checked against the page image.

column12: 0054 AOBA sighted BLUE
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.107 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Checked against the page image.

column12: 0058 course 100; signal "Enter by north entrance"
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.107 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Mikawa surprised to find BLUE; planned to avoid being seen. Checked against the page image.

column12: AUSTRALIA patrolling within the transport anti-submarine screen; Crutchley decided not to rejoin
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.147-148 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Crutchley told CTF 62 the enemy bound for Rekata Bay; was tired. Bates: he returned to AUSTRALIA about 0116 and chose to remain near the transports. Crutchley's own words quoted by Bates: not to rejoin in the dark with a few hours to 0500.

column12: about 0100 plane heard passing starboard going forward; Astoria sky control and Canberra also heard aircraft
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-Savo/USN-CN-Savo-4.html (Warnings)
column19: ONI: planes flew over at intervals for 1.5 h; reports reached the bridge but were not passed to gunnery control and no broadcast was made. Bates ch.IX: CANBERRA heard a Japanese plane overhead at intervals; no contact made.

column12: no radar contact recorded
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.110-111 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: BLUE's radar was operative (it had detected a plane) yet failed to detect the cruisers passing at about 5-10 nm (diagram: average 18,000 yd from CHOKAI between 0105 and 0120), the schooner at 9000 yd or YUNAGI at 12,400 yd. Reasons given: land interference, inexperience, fatigue, or SC radar being better against aircraft. Bates: "highly ineffective". The 8000-yd visibility given by BLUE. CTG 62.6 said BLUE's and RT's failure surprised him.

column12: about 0103 another "destroyer" bearing 159, taken for a destroyer
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.108 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: probably the schooner reported on 7 Aug. Mikawa at 0105 turned right to 150 and at 0108 signalled "Enter from south passage". Decided to withhold fire and keep silence. Checked against the page image.

column10: approx 24,000 yd away at 0100; 19,000 yd at 0105
column12: RALPH TALBOT about 24,000 yd away at 0100; CHOKAI about 19,000 yd at 0105
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.108 and 112 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: no contact; neither ship in visual range of the other and CHOKAI beyond radar range of RALPH TALBOT (SC radar). At 0120 closest approach was about 15,000-18,000 yd and that range was on YUNAGI only (neither saw each other). Checked against the page image.

column12: FURUTAKA obtained accurate bearings on the BLUE at 0121 and at 0126; Diagram E shows them 11,000 yards apart
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.111 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: The machine-read text prints 0116; the page image of p.110 reads 0121. Blue saw neither Furutaka nor the cruisers. Checked against the page image.

column12: RALPH TALBOT reached the western end of her patrol line at 0120 and reversed course; at this moment she was at her nearest point, 13,000 yards, to the Japanese Cruiser Force
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.112 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: The 13,000 yards was to Yunagi, last in the column. Neither ship sighted the other, and the cruisers did not sight Ralph Talbot. The machine-read text prints 15,000 and 18,000; the page image of p.112 reads 13,000. Checked against the page image.

column12: British Condition II modified; on guns half manned
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.125 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates says none of the commanding officers except Patterson's were awake; the others were asleep at the bridge level, relaxing after previous days. Fatigue: none thought night attack likely.

column12: Condition II; main battery guns loaded but not primed; captain asleep in emergency cabin
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.138-139 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: Vincennes and Astoria manned two guns in all three turrets; Quincy one forward turret and half the after turret; all turret guns loaded. All cruiser COs fully dressed and asleep in their emergency cabins adjoining their pilot houses. Group CO (Vincennes) wrote the enemy cruiser capability into his night orders and stressed alertness but did not tell other ships.

column12: Condition II; Material ZED; forward and after main battery fire-control radars out until just before contact (repaired)
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.138-140 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates and ONI ch.5: Astoria's AA battery fully manned; heat caused several cases of prostration. Astoria also unaware of warning because her TBS was in use for course orders.

column12: Condition II; Material YOKE; Ammunition Condition I
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.138 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: ONI ch.5. Bates: Quincy manned one forward turret and half the after turret. Quincy's radar picked up the first plane before midnight and later told to disregard contact.

column12: Condition II (to Condition I about 0145)
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.138 and 198 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Helm presumed Condition I by 0145 because she was alerted by flares and gunfire.

column12: Condition II (Condition I at 0150)
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.200 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)

column12: Condition TWO at 1754 8 Aug, Condition ONE at 1950; battle stations alerted 0045 9 Aug
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.76 and 107 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: Japanese conditions not known but probably similar to American. Bates says Japanese lookouts were rested and better trained for night; they saw targets before Allied lookouts did.

column12: BLUE unaware the Japanese had just passed; YUNAGI bearing 117 distant 12,400 yd; schooner 3000 yd
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.144 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Bates: BLUE completely unaware of the cruiser force, YUNAGI and the schooner.

column10: south of Savo, about 3000 yd south of the southern tip
column12: about 0134 destroyer bearing 76 left of base course (019 true), range about 3000 yd
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.114 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: AOBA and KAKO sighted her at 0135. Japanese trained guns but did not fire. JARVIS did not report because of apparent communication difficulties (damaged ship on her way out). Checked against the page image.

column12: at 0136 CANBERRA and CHICAGO in column bearing 120, range 12,500 yd
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.115 (ch.XI) (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: The page image reads 0136; one machine-read text layer prints 0156. The CHICAGO group had not sighted CHOKAI. Checked against the page image.

column12: 0137 cruiser bearing 060, range about 18,000 yd
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.115 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Longest visual sighting in the action. Bates: may have been silhouetted by fires at Tulagi or lightning; or told by floatplanes; or even imagined. Checked against the page image.

column12: 0138 four port torpedoes at range 10,000 yd, at CANBERRA and CHICAGO
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.115 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Torpedoes all missed. CANBERRA saw two on each side at 0143 (5 min later). Bates calls CHOKAI's firing odd as CANBERRA/CHICAGO were bow-on. Checked against the page image.

column12: 0139 destroyer 4 degrees on starboard bow, "great distance"; actual 9500 yd
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.115 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Checked against the page image.

column12: 0140 three ships (thought one battleship and two heavy cruisers, later London class), range about 9000 yd
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.115 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Mikawa at about the same time reported four ships bearing 120, range 7500 yd; PATTERSON bearing 130 at 5,500 yd reported at 0140.5. Checked against the page image.

column12: 0140 Vincennes changed course to 315; 0144 Astoria completed turn; Vincennes held course to 0200 order about 0145
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.140 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: ONI footnote 17: accounts contradictory on the time (Riefkohl: 0120; Heneberger: 0120; Topper: 0140). Bates 0140. The order to hold course occupied the TBS about 0145 and delayed warning receipt in Astoria.

column12: about 0143 sighted CANBERRA and CHICAGO at about 9000 yd; opened fire and launched four port torpedoes
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.117 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Also steering gear trouble at about 0144 caused by her own gunfire effect. Torpedoes missed (one or more passed under CHICAGO about 0147).

column12: about 0143 8-inch battery opened fire; no secondary battery
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.118 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Floatplane flares dropped just before: first sighted about 0143, at least four by 0145. CANBERRA first hit between 0144 and 0145; at least 24 hits by 0148 (CANBERRA XO claim; Bates doubts this by 0145).

column12: first flare about 0143; at least four by 0145; dropped to about 0225
column14: https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf ; Bates printed p.118 (archive.org scan of DTIC ADA003037; OCR text layer)
column19: Parachute flare burned about four minutes. Silhouetted the CHICAGO group (not the transports).

column12: Chicago sighted first flare at 0143 (ONI: 5 flares, bearing 160-170 relative)

column12: At 1905 Lt. Comdr. Leslie heard a plane of VT-3 report being over the target; it was over Roncador Reef; Leslie landed on Saratoga about 2333; Caldwell's 11 SBD's landed just after dark on Guadalcanal
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-ESols/USN-CN-ESolomons-4.html (printed p. 61)
column19: ONI times are Zone minus 11 1/2 (ONI ch.2 footnote 2), not converted. Enterprise planes did not find Ryujo or any ship. Four TBFs landed on Saratoga about 2200 with torpedoes jettisoned.

column12: When all our planes had returned or been given up for lost, Admiral Fletcher ordered a retirement to the south to refuel and to get the Enterprise started toward port and repairs. The Grayson was detached at 1756 to search astern

column5: abe vanguard force and kondo advance force
column12: Abe's vanguard force and Kondo's advanced force were steaming south to try to catch the U.S. carrier task forces in a surface battle, but they turned around at midnight without having made contact. Nagumo's main body, having taken heavy aircraft losses and being low on fuel, also retreated northward
column14: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Eastern_Solomons (wikitext read via action=raw; section named in note)
column19: Wikipedia gives no time zone; clock time kept as stated. Section 'Carrier action on 24 August'. Cites Frank 1990 p. 187, Hammel 1999 p. 320 (not seen). Earlier text: Abe's vanguard surged ahead of the carriers after 16:00.

column12: On the basis of these contacts, the enemy formation was spread out through an arc 60 to 80 miles wide, centered at about longitude 162 E, steering south
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-ESols/USN-CN-ESolomons-4.html (printed p. 55)

Not a statement that a vanguard force led the carriers; the combinedfleet Chikuma entry only places Chikuma and Tone in a 'Vanguard Force' that launched floatplanes.

column14: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Eastern_Solomons (wikitext read via action=raw; section named in note)

column12: At 1200, the attempt to land troops was cancelled by order of the Commander Out South Seas Force, and all ships retired to the Shortland Islands
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/AAF/USSBS/PTO-Campaigns/USSBS-PTO-7.html (Ch. VII, Battle of the Eastern Solomons, printed p. 111)

column12: We were ordered back. I think that it may have been because of the loss of the Ryujo and damage to the Shokaku. We did not have air support for a landing
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/AAF/USSBS/IJO/IJO-60.html (Nav No. 60, USSBS No. 252, Toyama, p. 252)

column12: Between 0245 and 0300 eight dive bombers were sent out from Henderson Field. Three located four enemy destroyers, scoring hits on one

column6: Tanaka convoy: large transport and heavy cruiser
column12: At 0835, about 125 miles to the north, this group came upon one large and three small transports, a heavy cruiser, light cruisers and four destroyers. They hit both the large (14,000-ton) transport and the heavy cruiser with 1,000-pound bombs
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/USN-CN-ESols/USN-CN-ESolomons-6.html (printed p. 71)
column19: ONI times are Zone minus 11 1/2 (ONI ch.2 footnote 2), not converted. ONI says eight dive bombers; USSBS says 12 located the force at 0935; combinedfleet says six SBDs at 0600; Wikipedia says 18 at 08:05. The cruiser is Jintsu per USSBS and combinedfleet. range_m converts the source's miles as nautical miles (unit not stated by the source).

column12: At dawn 12 Marine dive-bombers departed Henderson Field, locating the force at 0935. Jintsu took a bomb hit between No. 1 and No. 2 turrets which flooded the forward magazines; Tanaka transferred his flag to Kagero; Kinryu Maru was bombed and set on fire
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/AAF/USSBS/PTO-Campaigns/USSBS-PTO-7.html (Ch. VII, Battle of the Eastern Solomons, printed p. 111)
column19: USSBS gives no time zone; clock time kept as stated. Jintsu sent to Truk escorted by Suzukaze.

column12: At 0600, six USMC SBD dive-bombers attack the convoy. KINRYU MARU is hit and begins to sink. A 1000-lb bomb dropped by 1/Lt Baldinus of VMSB-232 strikes JINTSU's forecastle at 0805, starting fires and flooding forward magazines. Twenty-four crewmen killed
column14: http://www.combinedfleet.com/jintsu_t.htm (Tabular Record of Movement, entry for the date)
column19: combinedfleet gives no time zone; clock time kept as stated. 0600 and 0805 both given on this page; Wikipedia says Tanaka's 06:00 appears to be Japan Standard Time. Kinryu page: 'At 0600 six USMC SBDs ... KINRYU MARU hit by a 1,000-lb bomb amidships', Boston Maru near-missed.

column12: About 0700(-9), about 12 dive-bombers attacked us. The Jintsu was hit on the port side between number one and two turrets. One transport was also badly damaged, I think Kinryu Maru
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/AAF/USSBS/IJO/IJO-60.html (Nav No. 60, USSBS No. 252, Toyama)
column19: 0700 on the Japanese (zone -9) clock converted to 0900 zone minus 11 (two hours later) as the source gives the zone. Convoy about 100 miles north of Guadalcanal at 9 knots. range_m converts the source's miles as nautical miles (unit not stated by the source).

column12: At 08:05, 18 U.S. aircraft from Henderson Field attacked Tanaka's convoy, causing heavy damage to Jintsu, killing 24 crewmen, and knocking Tanaka unconscious. Kinryu Maru was also hit and eventually sank
column14: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Eastern_Solomons (wikitext read via action=raw; section named in note)
column19: Wikipedia gives no time zone; clock time kept as stated. Section 'Actions on 25 August'.

column12: At 1015 they released their bombs, hitting one cruiser or destroyer, with the result that it broke in two. Another cruiser was observed to be burning

column19: ONI times are Zone minus 11 1/2 (ONI ch.2 footnote 2), not converted. Identified later as destroyer Mutsuki. Claim of 'cruiser or destroyer' is a US observation.

column12: About 1015, while standing by this gutted and abandoned transport, the old destroyer Mitsuki [sic] sustained three hits from a flight of eight B-17s of the 11th Bombardment Group. At 1140 this destroyer sank

column12: At 1140 this destroyer sank, leaving only the destroyer Yayoi and Patrol Boats Nos. 1 and 2 to rescue the survivors
column14: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/AAF/USSBS/PTO-Campaigns/USSBS-PTO-7.html (Ch. VII, Battle of the Eastern Solomons, printed p. 111)
